calibration.example: Legible repair intake with clear labels, familiar layout and misplaced focus after an invalid number

primary_action.input: Tab through Name and Room to Submit permit; press Enter with both answers empty.
primary_action.expected: Explain both missing answers and focus the first field needing correction.
primary_action.observed: Displayed 'Enter your name.' and 'Choose Oak or Elm.' Focus moved visibly to Name.

A-1440.edge_observation: Typed Jamie, used Tab and ArrowRight to select Elm, then submitted. The confirmation showed Jamie and Elm and focused its heading. No edit control was visible.
A-1440.fact_check: Both required-answer messages and the confirmation values were observed. Actual permit issuance or persistence was not verified.
A-1440.strength: Clear field-level messages, strong focus indication and a compact aligned form.
A-1440.weakness: The confirmation offers no visible way to correct details, and the familiar form has little distinctive character.
A-1440.repair: Add an Edit details action that returns to the populated form; introduce a restrained library-specific visual detail.

primary_action.input: Tab to Submit permit and press Enter with both answers empty.
primary_action.expected: Explain both missing answers and focus Name.
primary_action.observed: Both field-level messages appeared and focus moved visibly to Name.

A-390.edge_observation: Keyboard entry of Jamie and selection of Elm produced a confirmation containing both values, with focus on the confirmation heading. No edit control was visible.
A-390.fact_check: The observed form and confirmation fit the 390 CSS-pixel viewport. Permit issuance and persistence were not verified.
A-390.strength: The stacked labels, full-width name field and error messages remain legible without visible clipping.
A-390.weakness: The confirmation has no visible correction route and leaves substantial unused space.
A-390.repair: Provide an Edit details action and use the confirmation space to make the next available step explicit.

primary_action.input: Tab through Name and Room to Confirm permit details; press Enter with both answers empty.
primary_action.expected: Explain both missing answers and focus Name.
primary_action.observed: Displayed 'Enter your name.' and 'Choose Oak or Elm.' Focus moved visibly to Name.

B-1440.edge_observation: Typed Jamie, selected Elm with ArrowRight and submitted. The confirmation showed Jamie and Elm, focused its heading and displayed an Edit details button. The edit button was not exercised.
B-1440.fact_check: The confirmation values and visible edit control were observed. Editing, permit issuance and persistence were not verified.
B-1440.strength: The wider, evenly sized room choices and clear section rules create an orderly form; the confirmation exposes a correction action.
B-1440.weakness: The desktop confirmation heading wraps in a narrow left column despite ample available space.
B-1440.repair: Give the confirmation heading more width while keeping the values and edit action aligned.

primary_action.input: Tab to Confirm permit details and press Enter with both answers empty.
primary_action.expected: Explain both missing answers and focus Name.
primary_action.observed: Both field-level messages appeared and focus moved visibly to Name.

B-390.edge_observation: Keyboard entry of Jamie and selection of Elm produced a confirmation containing both values. Focus moved to its heading and an Edit details button appeared; that button was not exercised.
B-390.fact_check: The observed form, errors and confirmation fit the 390 CSS-pixel viewport. Editing, permit issuance and persistence were not verified.
B-390.strength: Equal-width room choices, visible error text and a clear confirmation fit the mobile layout.
B-390.weakness: The visual language is orderly but generic, with the section rules doing most of the decorative work.
B-390.repair: Add a modest subject-specific detail while retaining the clear mobile spacing and controls.

preference.reason: Both designs completed the tested keyboard flow and explained both errors. B adds a visible Edit details action on confirmation and gives the room choices more balanced space, though the edit action itself remains untested.

decision: Both form drafts retrieved the same direction and passed the specified empty and corrected keyboard submissions. The control's extra Edit details action explained its higher usability rating. This result supplies a guard against breaking the task, not evidence of changed form routing.
